collection.description: A villager has been ill since the rains came.

ask.text:
(subject) has been ill since the rains came. (subject.He/She) is very old, and (subject.his/her) breathing rattles, and (subject.he/she) sleeps most of the day. (healer) has a strong remedy, bark from a tree on the far side of the island, but it's a hard journey, two days there and back.
(subject) doesn't want anyone making a fuss. "I've had a long life," (subject.he/she) says, each word slow. "Spend the two days with me instead."
Should (healer) make the journey for the bark, or stay?

c1o1.text: The bark tea is bitter as anything, and (subject) complains about every sip. But within a week, the rattle is gone, and within two (subject.he/she) is out in the sun again, and something about getting well seems to have taken years off (subject.his/her) face. "I told you not to make a fuss," (subject.he/she) says to (healer), and then hugs (healer.him/her) for a long time.

c1o2.text: (healer) runs into the village with the bark, and is met at the edge of the clearing by (subject)'s family. (subject) went that afternoon, peacefully, in (subject.his/her) sleep, with (subject.his/her) family around (subject.him/her). They tell (healer) that (subject) asked after (healer.him/her) at the end, and sent (healer.him/her) thanks, and not to be sad about the bark. The village buries (subject) in the sun, where (subject.he/she) liked to sit.

c1.text: (healer) leaves at dawn, running most of the way, and comes back on the second evening, scratched and limping, with a bundle of grey bark under (healer.his/her) arm...

c2o1.text: On the second night, the rattle in (subject)'s chest fades, slowly, and (subject.his/her) breathing grows easy. By the end of the week (subject.he/she) is sitting up, demanding fish. "See?" (subject.he/she) says. "No fuss. Just company." (healer) writes down in (healer.his/her) notes that sometimes the remedy is a person sitting beside the mat.

c2o2.text: (subject) sleeps most of the two days, but in the waking hours (subject.he/she) talks, slowly, about everything (subject.he/she) knows: which plants, which leaves, which old stories. (healer) listens and remembers it all. (subject) stays poorly for a long time, but comfortable. (healer) never forgets those two days, and is a better healer for every word.

c2.text: (healer) puts the bundle of travelling things away and sits down by the mat. For two days, (healer.he/she) and (subject)'s family take turns holding (subject)'s hand and telling (subject.him/her) the village news...
